states.why: The room is lit from the first note: a low blue on all four lamps.
Bars 4-6: the blue bed comes up a step where the score marks the build.
Bars 7-10: a steady blue bed; the brass carries the rhythm and amber carries the brass.
Bars 11-14: the inner pair holds blue under the voice alone.
Bars 15-21: a blue floor that climbs a step every bar under the pulses.
Bars 23-25: the drop arrives. Red and blue trade bars on a high floor, a hit on every beat by its measured weight.
Bars 26-28: the bass drops out and the singer leads. The room turns blue and the pairs swap at half speed.
Bar 29: bass and drums return, hardest in the section. Red home, floor higher.
Bars 31-34: drop 2. Red home, blue kicks, high floor.
Bar 34, beats 3-4: the floor comes down a step on the way into the backbeat bars.
Bars 35-37: the score shows a kick on every beat, heaviest on 2 and 4, drums thickening in bar 36, strings held. The same drive at a lower floor -- the drop breathing.
Bar 38: the whole band stops -- only the voice. A low blue floor.
Bar 39, beats 1-2: the band is back.
Bars 40-42: drop 3, the highest floor of the three.
Bar 43: the drums stop; a plain floor under the white climb.
The resolve: the brightest bed in the show under the colour wave.
The resolve: the brightest bed in the show under the colour wave. (continued across the section line)
The loudest twelve seconds on the record: red and white, the highest floor, a hit on every beat.
The loudest twelve seconds on the record: red and white, the highest floor, a hit on every beat. (continued across the section line)
The come-down: amber, the orchestra's colour from bars 7-10, returns as the room's colour.
113.0: the score marks a pause and the band is at 3%; the room dips with it.
The strings return; the amber bed with them.
The last entrance: amber settles a step.
The beat has gone; the room settles again.
The song ends in silence; the room fades to black with it.

gestures.why: Opening: a dim white pin, still. The head at rest is what makes its first move an event.
First vocal phrase (1.76-8.49 in the score): the inner pair lifts slowly through the line.
Two beats before the entrance the row swells white from the bed to full, so the hit at 13.83 is the top of a rise already under way.
The entrance: one smooth move to a new spot over the two beats of the swell, arriving exactly on 13.83.
Bars 4-10: still at its new spot.
The entrance at 13.83: one white beat at the top of the swell.
Third vocal phrase (15.90-17.22): the inner pair lifts again, into the tempo change at 17.75.
Bar 7: the horns punch just before beat 2 -- amber on the outer pair for one beat. Amber belongs to the brass.
Bar 8: the same punch, heavier, brighter.
Bar 9: the horns climb instead of punching; the outer pair swells amber with them into bar 10.
Bar 10: timpani and violins swell for the last beat and a half; the whole row swells amber into the hit.
Bars 11-14: dimming to a glow under the voice alone; off in the black beat.
The hit at 25.56 where the song changes section: full amber for two beats. Then amber is gone until the outro.
The lead-in phrase (27.02-33.75): the outer pair grows with the singer for six seconds.
Two beats before the riff, over the pause the score marks at 33.0, the row swells white.
One beat of nothing before the riff lands.
Bars 15-18, quarter notes: the whole row pulses red on every beat, a step brighter every bar, over the climbing blue floor.
Riff phrase one: the head glides slowly across the room over the whole phrase (8 seconds), at 40%, with a strobe pop on each downbeat.
The riff lands: one white beat.
Bars 17-18: the pushed off-beats join (at 0.56 of the beat, where the score hears them), on the inner pair, dimmer -- the pulse begins to double.
The joining piece: F at 41.02 -- the outer pair, red, full.
E at 41.30 -- the inner pair, red. The steps close inwards and phrase two lands on 41.76.
Riff phrase two: the head glides back over two bars to the spot the blackout will hold, brighter, popping on every beat.
Phrase two: half a beat of white on every downbeat, the heaviest note of the riff.
...and the outer pair, blue, takes every pushed off-beat.
Bars 19-20, eighth notes: the inner pair takes the beats...
Bar 21: the head holds and strobes on every beat as the room peaks.
Bar 21, sixteenths: red inner and blue outer in turn on every sixteenth, at full, the floor at its highest -- the fastest the room gets before the cut.
Bar 22: the whole band falls away at 47.7 (the score's pause at 48.0) -- full blackout, head included, as the volume shrinks.
"pa da ni sa ri": a hard white flick on each of the six syllables the score hears at 48.47, 48.64, 48.77, 48.93, 49.11, 49.33 -- the sudden transitions -- with black between them, then the drop.
The head flicks with the row, from where the blackout parked it.
Drop 1 lands: the impact.
…and the head at full, white, strobing, for that beat.
…held full white for the whole first beat.
Drop 1: the head glides from one side of the room to the other over two bars -- a slow pendulum on the bar grid, prism on, a strobe pop on each downbeat. The same pendulum in every drop.
52.76, the score's climax moment: one white beat.
…and to the centre for the singer.
Bars 26-28: centre, white, 45%, rising slowly through the singer's bars.
Bar 26, beat 1: one white beat marks the singer's entrance.
Bars 26-28, beat 4: a fast red run across the blue room, the pickup into the next bar.
Bar 29: back to red prism, gliding to the spot the blackout will hold.
Bar 29, beat 1: one white beat as the bass and drums come back.
Bar 30: the drums stop dead -- blackout for the first two beats.
Bar 30, beats 3-4: white flicks on the voice's notes (the score's melody), then drop 2.
The head flicks with the row, from where the blackout parked it.
Drop 2 lands.
…and the head at full, white, strobing, for that beat.
…held full white for the whole first beat.
Drop 2: the pendulum again, two bars a side.
…to the centre for the backbeat section.
Bars 35-37: a slow figure through the backbeat bars -- down to the left, across and up to the right, back to the centre -- one bar a side, dim white.
Bar 38: the head rises with the white climb.
Bar 38 from beat 2, where the voice re-enters alone: the row climbs white for three beats and lands on the band's return at 81.76.
Bar 39: red prism, gliding to the parked spot.
Bar 39, beat 3: blackout as the score's build moment at 83.26 approaches.
Bar 39, beat 4: white flicks, then drop 3.
The head flicks with the row, from where the blackout parked it.
Drop 3 lands.
…and the head at full, white, strobing, for that beat.
…held full white for the whole first beat.
Drop 3: the pendulum.
Bar 41, beat 1: one white beat.
…to the parked spot before bar 43.
Bar 43: the row climbs white for three beats into the resolve -- a release, not a drop, so it rises rather than flicks.
Bar 43: the head holds and strobes on the beat under the climb.
One black beat before the resolve.
The resolve lands: one beat of white.
The resolve: red, dim, drifting slowly to the centre under the waves.
The resolve: three slow colour waves, red over blue, two crossings each, turning round every two bars.
The climax: the pendulum at one bar a side, white prism at full, strobe pop on each downbeat -- the one place the head is the brightest thing in the room.
98.26: white strobe for two beats on the first big kick of the climax.
100.76: white strobe for three beats up to the single black beat before the loudest kick in the song.
…to the parked spot for the black beat.
One beat of nothing before the loudest kick.
102.76, the loudest kick: full red, falling away over four beats.
…to the centre for the come-down.
The breakdown at 109.76: the room turns amber at the drive's level and falls over four beats to the come-down bed.
The outro: one wide, slow sweep of the room in amber -- seven seconds to the far left...
The strings enter at 113.75 and swell for six seconds; the room swells amber with them up to the register shift at 120.29.
...seven seconds across to the far right as the strings swell...
The violins climb from 120.3; the room swells white into the last entrance.
The last entrance at 123.77 and the song's final peak at 124.5: amber, nearly full, held to where the band drops away at 126.
...and home to the centre, a touch brighter, for the last entrance. Off with the black beat at 127.23, and it stays off.
One beat of nothing where the beat drops away, as the score marks the rhythm change.
